Consequently an imported target's relative `inputs`/`outputs` and any files its command reads or writes resolve against the root config dir, so an imported target can write a file that a local target then consumes.    func expandString(s string, vars map[string]string, visiting map[string]bool) (string, error) {
       var b strings.Builder
       i := 0
       for i < len(s) {
           if i+1 < len(s) && s[i] == '$' && s[i+1] == '{' {
               end := strings.Index(s[i:], "}")
               if end == -1 {
                   return "", fmt.Errorf("unterminated variable reference in %q", s)
               }
               name := s[i+2 : i+end]
               if name == "" {
                   return "", fmt.Errorf("empty variable reference in %q", s)
               }
               if visiting[name] {
                   return "", fmt.Errorf("variable cycle detected: %q", name)
               }
               val, ok := vars[name]
               if !ok {
                   return "", fmt.Errorf("unresolved variable %q", name)
               }
               visiting[name] = true
               expanded, err := expandString(val, vars, visiting)
               if err != nil {
                   return "", err
               }
               delete(visiting, name)
               b.WriteString(expanded)
               i += end + 1
           } else {
               b.WriteByte(s[i])
               i++
           }
       }
       return b.String(), nil
   }
